video_title: Andre Drummond: how to stop Wemby, why he chose the Knicks + why everyone is injured now | E2S7

quotes.speaker: Mo Dakhil
quotes.summary_phrase: The high number of NBA injuries early this season
quotes.excerpt: the story of the season so far has been injuries. We are going to talk about those injuries.
quotes.quote: The story of the season so far has been injuries. We are going to talk about those injuries. Right now, Chet Holmgren, Ja Morant, Tyrese Haliburton, Anthony Edwards, Jaylen Brown, Jayson Tatum, Ben Simmons, Ben Sheppard, Jarred Vanderbilt, Aariq Hopoy, Brandon Ingram, Max Strus, Paolo Banchero, Jalen Suggs, Jalen Duren are all out with somewhat serious injuries. Some more serious than others, but nonetheless, some serious injuries. These are all guys that play valuable rotation minutes in the NBA. There was one night last week where 15% of the entire NBA was on the injury list. The season has just begun. For everyone who talks about they need to shorten the season, 82 games is too much, that's why these guys are getting hurt, well, we were a week and a half into the season and these guys started dropping like flies.

quotes.speaker: Mo Dakhil
quotes.summary_phrase: High pace and physical play contributing to NBA injuries
quotes.excerpt: the NBA is averaging the most possessions per game ever, right? So the pace of play is crazy.
quotes.quote: Kalen Cooper pointed out that it's a week into the season, the NBA is averaging the most possessions per game ever, right? So the pace of play is crazy. The shortest average possession length. You've heard me on the show talk about how frustrated I am that teams don't move the ball to find the best shot; they want to come up the floor and take the first shot available. They also have the highest average pickup distance, which I love, by the way. Guys picking up full court, I'm so here for it, but it does add wear and tear on the body. There's also the most possessions ever with at least three offensive players crashing the offensive glass rather than just dropping back on defense. I love the offensive rebounding, but that also adds wear and tear to the body.

quotes.speaker: Mo Dakhil
quotes.summary_phrase: Adam Silver on the impact of AAU programs on injuries
quotes.excerpt: a big part of his answer was about the AAU programs and the way in which players are developing
quotes.quote: I spoke to Adam Silver about this years ago. This was my first ever time being in a press conference with Adam Silver, and this is my 10th season covering the NBA. I said to him, 'What do you think is the cause for all of these injuries?' A big part of his answer was about the AAU programs and the way in which players are developing their games growing up and specializing in basketball to such a high level so early on in their young playing careers. These guys are doing NBA workouts with trainers. If you guys remember the interview we had with Drew Hanlen on season six of the Hoop Genius podcast, he was talking about when Jason Tatum was 13, he was in the gym working out with Jason Tatum every day. For a 13-year-old to be put through that, and I'm not saying Drew did anything wrong or Jason did anything wrong, but this is just showing the level of dedication that it takes for guys now to reach the NBA because there's so much competition for just 450 roster spots a season.

quotes.summary_phrase: Why Andre Drummond chose the Knicks in free agency
quotes.excerpt: I had a few different teams that reached out to me during free agency and you know the Knicks
quotes.quote:
Mo Dakhil: When you made that decision to go back closer to home, because you're from not far away from the New York area, right? When you made that decision, how much weighs in, because obviously there's the financial element, there's the basketball element, and then there's the personal happiness element of the thing. How do you weigh up between those three when you're choosing between different teams you play for at different stages of your career?

Andre Drummond: You know, I had a few different teams that reached out to me during free agency and you know the Knicks just made the most sense. I mean obviously I had a lot of contender teams that reached out and for me, what I'm trying to do in terms of being able to still play at a high level and play for a team that obviously just won, it was just a no-brainer to go back to the Nick, well go to the Knicks.

Andre Drummond: I mean I I love Philadelphia, I love playing there. My teammates are everything, you know they kept me sane while I was out there and our camaraderie was super dope. You know from the first year I was there to the second year we grew as a team. If they would have done those changes while I was still quote-unquote on roster, I don't think it would have changed. quotes.speaker: Andre Drummond
quotes.summary_phrase: Andre Drummond's defensive strategy against Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: Be physical with him. Get under him. Don't let him use his height and length.
quotes.quote:
Mo Dakhil: What's the game plan then when you have to guard him?

Andre Drummond: Be physical with him. Get under him. Don't let him use his height and length. I feel like right now he's still working on the the strength piece. So, I try to make it difficult for him, turn it into a track meet instead of him coming down and being able to survey the floor because like I said, he can pass the ball very well. He runs their offense to a T. So, it's like what do you do? What do you do? My thing is to try to get him from the beginning, as soon as he gets the ball at half court, try to press up into him, make him make him run, try to tire him out. I mean obviously he's still a very smart player and finds ways to still score, so just limiting the easy ones for him.

quotes.speaker: Andre Drummond
quotes.summary_phrase: Andre Drummond discusses his evolution into a three-point shooting threat
quotes.excerpt: I don't think it was a fact of wanting to start, it was more so having the faith

text_blocks.speaker: Mo Dakhil
text_blocks.text: You've added the three-pointer to your game now and people don't clock it because you've been around the league so long. They're like, 'Oh yeah, he ain't a shooter.' And then you just shoot it. When did you decide that you want to start expanding your game out to the three-point line?

text_blocks.speaker: Andre Drummond
text_blocks.text: I don't think it was a fact of wanting to start, it was more so having the faith in a coach to say, 'Shoot it.' He believes in me to shoot it and that's something I've worked on for the past decade. It was cool to come to Philadelphia, the first year I came to Philadelphia to play under Nick Nurse, he pulled me aside and said, 'Listen, I've seen you shoot the three-pointer before. I know you can shoot it. I want you to shoot it. Don't be dumb, don't shoot crazy shots, but if you're open, it's a good shot, shoot it.' So, the first year I played for Philly, I took a few threes and we had a conversation that it wasn't enough. I need to shoot them.
